chunks: What al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me of, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from Muhammad al-Halabi, who said:
I said to Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام: A man has become junub in his garment, and he has no garment other than it. He said: “He prays in it, and when he finds water, he washes it.”

It is not permissible for what is meant by this report to be anything except one who has sweated into the garment from janabah when it was from what is forbidden, because we have already explained that the state of janabah itself does not transfer to the garment. We also mentioned that the sweat of the junub does not make the garment najis, so no meaning remains upon which the report may be carried except the sweat of janabah from what is forbidden; thus we interpreted it accordingly, while it is also possible that the meaning in it is that some najasah had affected the garment, in which case he prays in it and then repeats, as we have explained.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, said: If a garment is washed of menstrual blood and a trace remains of it that washing does not remove, there is no harm in praying in it. It is recommended to dye it with something that removes its color, so he may pray in it with completeness of its taharah.
The verse indicates this, and it is His saying, Exalted is He:
“He has not placed upon you in the religion any hardship.”

The trace of menstrual blood may perhaps burden a person in trying to remove it, and that is not easy for him, so prayer in it has been permitted for him. As for what indicates the recommendation of dyeing the spot, it is as follows.

key_terms.أَجْنَبَ: entered the state of janabah (major ritual impurity)
key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: the state of major ritual impurity
key_terms.الْمَاءَ: water used to wash and purify the garment
key_terms.ثَوْبِهِ: his garment or clothing in which the ruling is being discussed
key_terms.دَمِ الْحَيْضِ: menstrual blood whose trace may remain after washing

ai.seo_question: Can one pray in a garment affected by janabah or with a remaining trace of menstrual blood after washing?
ai.summary: This report addresses legal rulings related to ritual purity, garments, and salat (prayer), especially when a person has limited clothing or when traces of menstrual blood remain after washing. It also cites the Quranic principle that Allah has not placed hardship in the religion, using it to support leniency where complete removal of a stain is difficult.
